SPACE.name: Space & Locomotion
SPACE.blurb: How the playable world is shaped and how you move through it.

CAM.name: Camera & Input
CAM.blurb: Where the eye sits and how intent reaches the character.

PROG.name: Progression & Persistence
PROG.blurb: What the game remembers about you between deaths and sessions.

NARR.name: Narrative
NARR.blurb: How fiction is delivered and how much of it the player authors.

CBT.name: Combat & Conflict
CBT.blurb: The grammar of hitting, blocking, aiming, and dying.

SIM.name: Physics & Simulation
SIM.blurb: When the world obeys rules instead of scripts.

WORLD.name: World Systems
WORLD.blurb: Time, weather, ecology, and NPCs that live without you.

MP.name: Multiplayer & Social
MP.blurb: Other humans, from the same couch to the same shard.

UI.name: Interface & Meta
UI.blurb: Maps, markers, logs, and the scaffolding around play.

PROC.name: Procedural Generation
PROC.blurb: Content authored by algorithm rather than by hand.

ECON.name: Economy & Business Model
ECON.blurb: How the game asks to be paid, and what that does to design.

STLTH.name: Stealth & Perception
STLTH.blurb: Enemies that can fail to notice you — and the systems that model it.

CREATE.name: Creation & Modding
CREATE.blurb: Handing the authoring tools to the player.

STRAT.name: Strategy & Tactics
STRAT.blurb: Commanding many things at once, in real time or in turns.

RHYTHM.name: Rhythm & Audio
RHYTHM.blurb: Sound as a mechanic rather than a garnish.

features.name: Object Collision As Verb
features.desc: Two things occupy the same space and something happens. Every act of hitting, landing, blocking, or dying in the medium descends from this single primitive.

features.name: Single-Screen Arena
features.desc: The whole world fits in one frame. Constraint, not limitation: it forces every element on screen to matter.

features.name: Wraparound Topology
features.desc: Exit the right edge, enter the left. The first non-Euclidean playspace, and the ancestor of every looping world.

features.name: Flip-Screen Room Graph
features.desc: The world becomes a graph of discrete rooms rather than one arena. Dungeon design, level design, and the map screen all start here.

features.name: Continuous Scrolling Playfield
features.desc: The camera decouples from the world and the world becomes larger than the screen. Arguably the single most consequential spatial idea before 3D.

features.name: Parallax Depth Layers
features.desc: Background layers scroll at different rates, faking depth on hardware with none. The first cheap illusion of a third dimension.

features.name: Isometric Projection
features.desc: A fixed oblique angle that reads as 3D while remaining 2D data. Survives today in tactics games and ARPGs.

features.name: Sprite-Scaling Pseudo-3D
features.desc: Sprites grow as they approach. Depth without polygons — the road-racer and rail-shooter lineage.

features.name: First-Person Vector Space
features.desc: The camera enters the world at eye level. Wireframe, monochrome, and the direct ancestor of every FPS.

features.name: Momentum-Based Platform Control
features.desc: Acceleration, skid, variable jump arc. The player learns a physical vocabulary rather than a binary one.

features.name: Ability-Gated Interlocked Map
features.desc: The map is one connected space locked by capabilities, not doors. Progression becomes spatial rather than linear.

features.name: Rotating Ground Plane
features.desc: A texture-mapped floor that rotates and scales in hardware. The bridge between sprite tricks and real 3D.

features.name: Raycast Corridor 3D
features.desc: Textured walls at speed on consumer hardware. First-person space stops being a novelty and becomes a genre.

features.name: True Polygonal Free-Look Space
features.desc: Real geometry, real rooms above rooms, and a camera free on all axes. The 3D world stops lying about itself.

features.name: Analog Free-Roam 3D Movement
features.desc: 360 degrees of graded movement in third person, with a camera that must be solved as a design problem. The grammar nearly all 3D action games still use.

features.name: Hub-and-Spoke World Access
features.desc: A central space that fans out into levels, letting the player choose order and revisit. The seed of nonlinear campaign structure.

features.name: Non-Euclidean Portal Space
features.desc: Player-authored topology: two surfaces become one. Space itself becomes the puzzle object.

features.name: Seamless Streaming Open World
features.desc: A contiguous city with no loading seams, traversable at will. Converts 'levels' into 'places' and makes the map the content.

features.name: Systemic Climbable Surfaces
features.desc: Architecture annotated as a climbing grid, so the whole skyline becomes navigable. Open worlds gain a Z axis.

features.name: Grapple & Tether Traversal
features.desc: Momentum-preserving swing or tether movement that makes crossing the map its own reward loop.

features.name: First-Person Parkour Flow
features.desc: Traversal as the primary verb, read through a first-person body with visible limbs and momentum.

features.name: Climb-Anything Stamina Traversal
features.desc: Every surface is climbable and the only limit is a resource. Removes the designer's invisible walls and returns route-finding to the player.

features.name: Planetary-Scale Streaming
features.desc: Surface to orbit to interstellar with no cut. Scale itself becomes the spectacle.

features.name: Fixed Cinematic Camera
features.desc: Pre-authored camera angles in a 3D space. Cheap on hardware, expensive on nerves — the horror lineage runs through it.

features.name: Trailing Follow Camera
features.desc: A camera that is itself a character with collision and intent. The first serious attempt to solve 3D viewing as a system.

features.name: Graded Analog Input
features.desc: Input stops being on/off. Walk, jog, sprint, and precise aim become expressible with one thumb.

features.name: Dual-Analog Move + Look
features.desc: Left stick moves, right stick looks. Ridiculed on arrival, canonized by Halo, and now the default control scheme of the medium.

features.name: Contextual Lock-On Targeting
features.desc: Z-targeting fused camera and combat: the system decides what matters and orbits it. Made 3D melee legible.

features.name: Over-the-Shoulder Aim
features.desc: Camera pinned behind the shoulder with the crosshair in the world. Introduced alongside cover in kill.switch, then canonized by Resident Evil 4 two years later.

features.name: Iron-Sight Aim-Down-Sights
features.desc: A second aiming mode trading mobility and view for accuracy. The core risk/reward toggle of the modern shooter.

features.name: Directed In-Engine Camera Language
features.desc: Film grammar — cuts, dollies, framing — applied to a live engine, so gameplay and cinema share one camera.

features.name: Photo Mode
features.desc: A camera the player owns. Turns the world into a subject and the audience into cinematographers.

features.name: Haptic Force Feedback
features.desc: Information delivered through the hands. A channel with no screen budget and no localization cost.

features.name: Spatial Motion Input
features.desc: The controller's position in the room becomes the input. Briefly made the medium legible to people who had never held a gamepad.

features.name: Direct Touch Manipulation
features.desc: No cursor, no avatar — the finger is the input device. The control scheme that made a billion-player market possible.

features.name: Room-Scale VR Presence
features.desc: Head and hands tracked in real space, so the camera is the player's neck. The most radical revision of the camera problem since 1996.

features.name: Numeric Score
features.desc: The first thing a game ever remembered. Every progression system is a descendant of the impulse to keep a number.

features.name: Lives and Continues
features.desc: Failure becomes a budget rather than an ending. Introduces the tension between challenge and access that arcades monetized.

features.name: Persistent High-Score Table
features.desc: Three initials in battery-backed RAM: the first persistent player identity and the first leaderboard.

features.name: Permadeath Run Structure
features.desc: Death erases the save. Makes every decision load-bearing and turns a session into a story.

features.name: Experience Points and Levels
features.desc: Ported from tabletop: repeated action converts into permanent capability. The economic engine of the RPG and, eventually, of nearly everything else.

features.name: Character Classes
features.desc: Pre-bundled capability sets that trade breadth for identity. Reappears as the shooter's 'loadout' and the MOBA's 'champion'.

features.name: Checkpoint Respawn
features.desc: Failure rewinds to a marker instead of the start. The single biggest lever on a game's felt difficulty.

features.name: Password Continuation
features.desc: State encoded as a string the player carries. Persistence without hardware — and an accidental early modding surface.

features.name: Battery-Backed Save File
features.desc: The cartridge remembers. Games can now be longer than one sitting, which invents the modern campaign.

features.name: New Game Plus
features.desc: Carry your power into a fresh run. Replay stops being repetition and becomes a different game.

features.name: Branching Skill Tree
features.desc: Progression as a spatial choice with opportunity cost. Now standard equipment in genres that have nothing else in common.

features.name: Colour-Coded Loot Rarity
features.desc: White, blue, gold. A one-glance value language that became the medium's most portable UI convention — and its most exploitable.

features.name: Numeric Gear Power Treadmill
features.desc: Items reduced to a single ascending number, enabling endless content tiers and endless obsolescence.

features.name: Perk-Based Loadout Customization
features.desc: Players build their own class from unlockable modifiers. RPG progression injected into the competitive shooter.

features.name: Prestige Reset-for-Status
features.desc: Voluntarily surrender your progress for a symbol. Progression becomes theatre, and the treadmill becomes infinite.

features.name: Run-Persistent Meta-Progression
features.desc: You lose the run but keep something. The compromise that made roguelikes mass-market and created the roguelite.

features.name: Bonfire Checkpoint & Currency Risk
features.desc: Rest resets the world; death drops your currency where you fell and gives you one chance to retrieve it. Risk expressed entirely through save design.

features.name: Attract-Mode Premise
features.desc: Interstitial vignettes with no interaction, purely to establish character. Fiction enters the arcade sideways.

features.name: In-Engine Cutscene
features.desc: The engine takes the controller away to tell you something. Contested ever since, and never abandoned.

features.name: Quick-Time Event
features.desc: Interaction reduced to a timed prompt over authored spectacle. The cheapest possible bridge between cinema and play.

features.name: Branching Dialogue Trees
features.desc: Conversation as a navigable structure. Makes the player a participant in the fiction rather than its audience.

features.name: Explicit Morality Axis
features.desc: The game scores your ethics. Radical in 1985, reduced to a blue/red button by 2007, and still unsolved.

features.name: Full-Motion Video
features.desc: Filmed actors on optical media. A commercial dead end that permanently raised production-value expectations.

features.name: Environmental Storytelling
features.desc: The level is the narrator. Corpses, graffiti, and arrangement carry plot without stopping play.

features.name: Found Audio Log
features.desc: Recorded voices from the dead, consumed while moving. Solved the 'story without cutscenes' problem so well it became a cliché.

features.name: Full Voice Performance
features.desc: Every line performed. Doubles the emotional bandwidth and permanently multiplies the cost of narrative iteration.

features.name: Companion Approval
features.desc: NPCs keep a private opinion of you that gates content and affection. The mechanic that turned party members into the reason people replay.

features.name: Faction Reputation
features.desc: Not good or evil but 'whose side'. Converts moral choice into a systems-legible resource with real world-state consequences.

features.name: Consequential Branching Endgame
features.desc: Accumulated choices reshape the final act rather than a slide at the end. Makes the morality axis mechanically honest.

features.name: Cinematic Dialogue Wheel
features.desc: Paraphrased intent selected radially so the camera never has to stop moving. Traded precision for cinematic continuity.

features.name: Player-Agency Narrative Twist
features.desc: The story's subject is the player's own compliance. The medium turning its one unique property — interactivity — into theme.

features.name: Hit Points
features.desc: Damage as a depleting pool rather than instant death. Makes combat a negotiation instead of a coin flip.

features.name: Chained Combo Strings
features.desc: Inputs that link into uninterruptible sequences — discovered in a bug, kept because it created a depth ceiling nobody had designed.

features.name: Cancels and Super Meter
features.desc: A resource earned by fighting well and spent on decisive moments. Gives the fighting game its comeback drama.

features.name: Parry and Riposte Window
features.desc: Defense as an aggressive, high-risk timing act. Migrates out of fighting games into action, Souls, and eventually everything.

features.name: Directional Attack and Block
features.desc: Attacks and guards have geometry. The root of the modern 'melee as reading' school.

features.name: Weapon Durability Decay
features.desc: Tools are consumables. Converts inventory from hoard to budget and forces improvisation.

features.name: Ability Cooldown Economy
features.desc: Power gated by time rather than resource. The clock that MOBAs, hero shooters, and action-RPGs all now run on.

features.name: Player-Controlled Bullet Time
features.desc: Time as a spendable resource for aiming. Gives the player directorial control over their own action scene.

features.name: Regenerating Health
features.desc: Disengage and recover. Replaces the health-pack scavenger hunt with a rhythm of pressure and retreat — and quietly reshapes level design.

features.name: Constrained Weapon Loadout
features.desc: Carry two, choose deliberately. Turns pickups into decisions and makes the sandbox readable.

features.name: Snap-to-Cover Combat
features.desc: Geometry becomes a verb. Perfected by Gears of War and imitated for a decade, for better and worse.

features.name: Learnable Recoil Patterns
features.desc: Weapon spray is deterministic, so mastery is memorizable. The invisible skill curve underneath competitive FPS.

features.name: Stamina Action Economy
features.desc: Every offensive and defensive act costs from one shared bar. Makes deliberateness a mechanic and panic a punishable state.

features.name: Poise and Stagger Break
features.desc: A second hidden health bar for balance. Creates the aggression/patience dilemma at the heart of the soulslike.

features.name: Contextual Execution
features.desc: A close-quarters kill that costs vulnerability and buys spectacle. Risk purchased with time, paid in theatre.

features.name: Deflect-Focused Posture Combat
features.desc: Deflection replaces dodging as the core defensive verb, converting combat from spacing into rhythm.

features.name: Ragdoll Physics
features.desc: Bodies simulated rather than animated on death. The first widely visible sign the world had a physics engine underneath it.

features.name: Rigid-Body Puzzle Physics
features.desc: Mass, buoyancy, and leverage as puzzle vocabulary. Physics stops being decoration and becomes the solution space.

features.name: Physics Manipulation Tool
features.desc: A device that grants the player direct control over the simulation. One object that teaches an entire system.

features.name: Destructible Geometry
features.desc: Level geometry that can be removed. Undermines the designer's assumption of a fixed floor plan, which is precisely the appeal.

features.name: Editable Voxel Terrain
features.desc: The world as a uniform grid of removable, placeable matter. The simplest possible world model, and the most generative.

features.name: Soft-Body Deformation
features.desc: Structures that bend and crumple rather than swapping to a damage model. Simulation fidelity as spectacle.

features.name: High-Fidelity Vehicle Physics
features.desc: Tyre load, weight transfer, and drivetrain modelled seriously. Turned racing games into an equipment hobby.

features.name: Flight Simulation
features.desc: Aerodynamics modelled for their own sake, with no score. The earliest commercial argument that simulation is itself the entertainment.

features.name: Propagating Fire and Fluids
features.desc: Fire that spreads with wind and terrain. An emergent hazard the designer cannot fully script and the player can weaponize.

features.name: Systemic Elemental Chemistry
features.desc: Fire, wind, water, metal, and electricity interacting by rule everywhere. Puzzle solutions the designers never enumerated.

features.name: Day/Night Cycle
features.desc: The world keeps time whether or not you act. The first hint that a game world exists independently of the player.

features.name: NPC Daily Schedules
features.desc: Characters sleep, work, and eat on their own clocks. Creates the illusion of a society rather than a set of quest dispensers.

features.name: Dynamic Weather
features.desc: Simulated, sometimes forecast-driven weather. Atmosphere that the player cannot predict and the designer cannot stage.

features.name: Survival Needs Clock
features.desc: The food clock: standing still is itself a losing move. Pressure without an enemy on screen.

features.name: Crafting From Gathered Materials
features.desc: Players manufacture goods from raw inputs. Gives non-combat play an economy and the world a supply chain.

features.name: Free-Form Base Building
features.desc: Permanent player-authored structures inside the play space. Turns a level into property.

features.name: Radiant / Generated Activity
features.desc: The world generates its own low-level content and incidents. Infinite filler, and occasionally something no writer would have dared.

features.name: Dynamic AI Director
features.desc: An invisible system pacing tension by spawning against your emotional state. Difficulty becomes dramaturgy.

features.name: Simulated Ecology
features.desc: Animals and townsfolk with territory, routine, and memory. Fidelity spent on things the player may never notice — which is the point.

features.name: Procedural Nemesis Hierarchy
features.desc: Enemies who remember, get promoted, and taunt you about last time. The strongest case yet that character can be generated.

features.name: Same-Screen Two-Player
features.desc: The original multiplayer: one screen, two humans, immediate social consequence. Still undefeated for pure legibility.

features.name: Split-Screen Simultaneous
features.desc: Two independent viewports, one room. Enables asymmetric information between people sitting next to each other.

features.name: Networked Deathmatch
features.desc: Four players, one network, no rules. Invented competitive PC gaming and, incidentally, a great deal of IT policy.

features.name: Internet Client-Server Play
features.desc: Authoritative servers and client prediction over unreliable links. The engineering that makes everything after it possible.

features.name: Persistent Shared World
features.desc: A world that continues without you, with an economy and a society. The most ambitious idea the medium has attempted.

features.name: Player Guilds and Clans
features.desc: Formal in-game institutions with membership and hierarchy. Retention through obligation to other people.

features.name: Coordinated Raid Encounters
features.desc: Choreographed fights requiring dozens of synchronized players. The medium's only real orchestra.

features.name: Drop-In Co-op Campaign
features.desc: The story mode, but with a friend and no ceremony. Quietly one of the most requested features in the medium.

features.name: Automated Skill Matchmaking
features.desc: Party, rank, playlist, go. Removed server browsers and made competitive play a console-scale product.

features.name: Persistent Multiplayer Progression
features.desc: Losing still pays. The single most consequential monetization-adjacent design decision of the last twenty years.

features.name: Asynchronous Invasion & Messages
features.desc: Other players appear as bloodstains, scrawled warnings, and sudden hostile intrusions. Multiplayer as weather.

features.name: Lane-Push Objective Structure
features.desc: Fixed lanes, creep waves, towers, a base to destroy. A mod's map layout became one of the largest genres on earth.

features.name: Shrinking-Circle Battle Royale
features.desc: Scavenge, avoid, and let a closing boundary force the endgame. Solves the deathmatch pacing problem with geometry.

features.name: Cross-Platform Play
features.desc: Platform walls fall so the friend list can stay whole. A business achievement more than a technical one.

features.name: Non-Verbal Ping Communication
features.desc: A contextual pointing grammar that conveys intent without voice. Accessibility, localization, and harassment reduction in one feature.

features.name: Asymmetric Multiplayer Roles
features.desc: Sides with entirely different rulesets, goals, and cameras. Balance becomes an ongoing negotiation rather than a state.

features.name: Extraction Risk/Reward Loop
features.desc: Bring gear in, lose it if you die, keep it if you leave. Reintroduces stakes to online shooters.

features.name: In-Game Automap
features.desc: The game draws the map as you explore it. Externalizes spatial memory and makes large levels tractable.

features.name: Fog of War
features.desc: Information itself becomes a resource to contest. The foundation of every strategy game's scouting layer.

features.name: Persistent Minimap / Radar
features.desc: A live corner map of threats and space. Reduces cognitive load and, in competitive play, becomes the primary display.

features.name: Spatial Inventory Grid
features.desc: Carrying capacity as a packing puzzle. Makes 'what do I leave behind' a real decision.

features.name: Quest Journal
features.desc: The game tracks what you were told. Enables nonlinear questing without a notepad next to the keyboard.

features.name: Waypoint Objective Marker
features.desc: A dot that says go here. Made open worlds navigable and, arguably, made exploring them unnecessary.

features.name: Selectable Difficulty
features.desc: The player declares their own contract with the game up front. Access and challenge stop being the same axis.

features.name: Platform Achievements
features.desc: A cross-game persistent score attached to an account. The arcade high-score table rebuilt as a platform-wide identity.

features.name: Diegetic HUD-less Interface
features.desc: Health on the spine, ammo on the gun. Information without breaking the frame — immersion as an interface constraint.

features.name: Comprehensive Accessibility Suite
features.desc: Granular remapping, audio cues, high contrast, aim assist tiers. Difficulty reframed as one of many access axes.

features.name: Procedurally Generated Levels
features.desc: The level is generated at runtime, so no one — including the designer — has played it. Infinite content from finite rules.

features.name: Seeded Procedural Universe
features.desc: Eight galaxies from a few bytes of seed. Establishes that scale can be computed rather than stored.

features.name: Procedural Loot Tables
features.desc: Randomized affixes on generated items. The slot-machine core of the entire ARPG genre.

features.name: Emergent Generated History
features.desc: Centuries of simulated world history before you place a single tile. Story as a simulation output.

features.name: Infinite Chunked World
features.desc: The world generates ahead of you forever. Exploration without an edge, and a shareable seed as a social object.

features.name: Coin-Op Difficulty Economy
features.desc: Difficulty tuned to extract another quarter. The first time monetization directly authored the difficulty curve — and not the last.

features.name: Retail Expansion Pack
features.desc: More content for an owned game, sold separately. Establishes the game as an ongoing product rather than a finished object.

features.name: Downloadable Content
features.desc: Content delivered post-launch over the network, at any size. Horse armour taught the industry exactly how small a unit could be sold.

features.name: Season Pass Bundle
features.desc: Pre-purchase of unspecified future content. Revenue moved before the content exists.

features.name: Free-to-Play Service Model
features.desc: Zero price at the door, revenue from a minority of players. The arcade model with an unlimited coin slot.

features.name: Cosmetic-Only Monetization
features.desc: Sell identity, not power. The compromise that made free-to-play acceptable to competitive players.

features.name: Randomized Loot Box
features.desc: Paid randomized rewards. The most profitable and most regulated idea in the medium's commercial history.

features.name: Seasonal Battle Pass
features.desc: A time-limited progression track bought up front. Replaced the loot box as the industry's default by trading randomness for obligation.

features.name: Live-Service Seasonal Content
features.desc: The game is a schedule. Content, narrative, and economy all arrive on a calendar and expire on one.

features.name: Paid Early Access Development
features.desc: Sell the unfinished game and develop with the audience inside the tent. Financing and playtesting merged into one act.

features.name: Mobile Free-to-Play
features.desc: Session-length design around energy timers and in-app purchase. By revenue, the dominant form of the medium.

features.name: Line-of-Sight Detection
features.desc: Enemies that can fail to see you. Introduces the idea that the AI has a state of knowledge distinct from the game's.

features.name: Graduated Alert States
features.desc: Unaware, suspicious, alerted, searching, resolved. Failure becomes a recoverable state instead of a restart.

features.name: Explicit Detection Feedback
features.desc: The player is shown what the AI knows. Makes an invisible system fair, and stealth teachable.

features.name: Light-and-Shadow Stealth
features.desc: Illumination and sound as measured, readable resources. Turns lighting from art direction into level design.

features.name: Systemic Solution Space
features.desc: Consistent interacting systems instead of authored solutions, so problems have answers the designers never listed. The immersive sim's founding contract.

features.name: Social / Crowd Stealth
features.desc: Hiding in plain sight through behaviour rather than geometry. Stealth moves from the shadows into the daylight.

features.name: Diegetic 3D Audio Information
features.desc: Footstep material, distance, and occlusion carry real tactical data. The ear as a primary sensor.

features.name: Bundled Level Editor
features.desc: The authoring tool ships in the box. The player becomes a designer without asking permission.

features.name: Open Data Formats and Mod SDK
features.desc: WADs, then source. Created an unpaid apprenticeship pipeline that produced Counter-Strike, DotA, PUBG, and a generation of studios.

features.name: User-Content Marketplace
features.desc: Players build, publish, and get paid inside the platform. The game becomes an economy of games.

features.name: In-Game Creation Suite
features.desc: Authoring with a gamepad, from inside the fiction. Creation as play rather than as a separate tool.

features.name: Replay Capture and Sharing
features.desc: The match is recorded as data and re-cameraable. Turns play into shareable media and seeds the clip economy.

features.name: Real-Time Base and Unit Production
features.desc: Harvest, build, produce, attack — under continuous time pressure. The template every RTS since has argued with.

features.name: Turn-Based Grid Tactics
features.desc: Positioning on a grid with persistent, levelling units. Consequence measured in squares.

features.name: Turn-Based 4X Empire
features.desc: Explore, expand, exploit, exterminate across millennia. The strategy game as historical argument.

features.name: Tower Defense Lane Denial
features.desc: Static defenses against pathing waves — born as a custom map, spun out into a genre of its own.

features.name: Deck-Building Run Progression
features.desc: Your build is a deck assembled during the run. Merged the card game with the roguelike and created a decade of imitators.

features.name: Adaptive Dynamic Music
features.desc: Score that transitions on the beat to follow player action. Music becomes responsive rather than looped.

features.name: Beat-Matched Input
features.desc: Scoring judged against a musical grid. Time itself becomes the difficulty axis.

features.name: Scrolling Note Highway
features.desc: Future input rendered as approaching geometry. A sight-reading interface anyone can learn in ten seconds.

features.name: Instrument Peripheral
features.desc: A dedicated physical object that makes the fantasy tactile. Hardware as the whole pitch.

features.name: Rhythm-Locked Action
features.desc: Every action must land on the beat, fusing a music game with a dungeon crawl. Two genres solving each other's pacing problems.
